business_scope.primary_industry_name: Professional Multilingual Translation and Media Dubbing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, enacted December 20, 1962, as amended, particularly Articles 288 through 317 governing incorporation and registration of a stock corporation (Chusik Hoesa): Article 288 (incorporator requirements), Article 289 (execution of articles of incorporation), Article 292 (notarization of articles), Article 295 (subscription of shares), Article 312 (payment of subscription price), Article 313 (appointment of initial directors and statutory auditor), and Article 317 (registration of incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, operated under the Supreme Court of Korea; online filings are accepted through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Corporation filed under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act and Article 66 of the Rules on Registration of Non-Contentious Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the total subscription price of all shares issued at incorporation must be fully paid before the incorporation registration is granted. The payment must be made by depositing the funds into a bank or licensed securities company account opened in the name of the proposed company, and the deposit confirmation certificate must be submitted to the court registry. The deposited funds must remain blocked until after registration; after registration, the depositary institution must verify the corporation registration certificate before releasing the funds. In-kind contributions must be appraised by a court-appointed appraiser and the relevant assets must be fully transferred before the registration deadline.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY. The Board of Directors of the Company being duly convened and a quorum being present, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and unanimously adopted by all directors present and voting. RESOLVED, that the subscribed and paid-in share capital of the Company, fully contributed by the founding shareholders and verified by the deposit certificate issued by the depositary bank or securities company, is hereby ratified, accepted, and confirmed, and that all prior subscription agreements, contribution schedules, and in-kind valuation reports executed by the incorporators are ratified and adopted as binding obligations of the Company. RESOLVED, that the Board authorizes the opening, operation, and maintenance of corporate bank accounts, foreign currency accounts, electronic banking accounts, and online payment platform accounts with licensed banks and authorized financial institutions. The Chief Executive Officer together with the Chief Financial Officer, or either of them acting alone with the other's written mandate, shall execute account opening applications, signature cards, mandates, SWIFT or BIC instructions, and payment rail onboarding documents necessary for wire transfers and international settlement. RESOLVED, that the registered office located at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, within the jurisdiction of the competent District Court Registration Office, is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory seat, principal place of business, and legal domicile for service of process, official notices, tax correspondence, and shareholder notices. The Board authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to execute lease documents and to notify the registration office and tax authorities of any future relocation of the registered office. RESOLVED, that the following persons be and hereby are appointed to statutory office until their successors are elected at the next ordinary general meeting of shareholders: one director as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director, one director as Chief Financial Officer, and one statutory auditor, each having consented in writing to serve and to perform all fiduciary duties imposed by the Korean Commercial Act and the Company's Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED, that the officers of the Company are instructed to file the corporation registration with the competent District Court Registry, to file the business registration and tax identification documents with the National Tax Service, to obtain the necessary permits for the registered office, and to execute and deliver all documents, powers of attorney, governmental filings, electronic filing credentials, employment registrations, and bank mandate forms necessary to place the Company in full legal operation. RESOLVED, that any lawful action taken by the incorporators or officers prior to this meeting in furtherance of the incorporation of the Company is hereby ratified, approved, confirmed, and adopted as the act of the Company. The foregoing resolutions are effective immediately and may be carried out by any one authorized officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share subscription, capital contribution, and pre-incorporation deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank or licensed securities company acting as depositary institution for the proposed corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators shall convene or be represented by proxy and shall execute the incorporation subscription statement, agreeing on the number of shares, par value, and total capital. Each incorporator shall subscribe to at least one share and the entire number of shares to be issued at incorporation must be subscribed. The full amount of subscription price must be paid into a corporate-capacity deposit account opened in the proposed company name at a domestic bank or licensed securities company, with a certificate of deposit issued to the incorporators. If contribution is in kind, the applicable property must be appraised by a court-appointed appraiser with a report attached. The certificate is held in escrow until after incorporation registration. During this phase, no official government approval is needed, but documents must be drafted in advance to avoid correction orders.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription statement signed by all incorporators
Identification or passport copies and seal certificates of incorporators
Power of attorney if an agent will act for any incorporator
Capital deposit account application form
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
Proposed list of initial directors and statutory auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary institution rejects the pre-incorporation account because of a name mismatch or incomplete seal certificate, correct the proposed corporate name or signature documentation and reopen the account. If an in-kind valuation is challenged, obtain a supplementary appraisal or reduce the stated capital to the appraised fair market value.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public commissioned under the Korean Notary Act in the district where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notarized Articles of Incorporation are the constitutive document of a Chusik Hoesa. The incorporators shall submit the finalized Articles to a notary public and sign or affix their seals in the presence of the notary. The notary must verify the statutory contents, including the corporate purpose, trade name, total authorized shares, par value, issued shares, registered office address, method of public notice, names and identification of incorporators, capital contribution arrangement, and the appointed initial directors and statutory auditor. If the Company will issue only one class of shares, that fact must be stated. Any attorney-in-fact must present a notarized power of attorney. The notary retains one certified copy and returns the original notarized Articles for use in the registration application.
required_dossiers: Final executed draft of the Articles of Incorporation
Passports or national identification of all incorporators
Personal seal certificates or authorized signature specimens
Notarized power of attorney for any proxy
Written consent to appointment of each director and statutory auditor
Lease agreement or owner consent for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses notarization because of omission of a statutory item, amend the Articles by unanimous incorporation act and resubmit. If the corporate object includes regulated business activities, split the object clauses or delete the unlicensed regulated activity before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The application for incorporation registration must be filed at the Registry Division of the district court where the registered office is located within two weeks after notarization of the Articles, under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act. The authorized representative shall submit the statutory application form, the original notarized Articles, the certificate of payment for the subscription price or an in-kind contribution appraisal report, minutes or written resolutions documenting the appointment of directors and statutory auditor, and written consent to appointment signed by each officer. The registration officer reviews whether the documentation is complete, whether capital contributions have been paid, and whether the corporate name is not identical to an existing registered company. Upon approval, the Company is legally established from the moment of registration, and the Registry issues the Corporation Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Statutory application for registration of establishment
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital contribution deposit certificate or in-kind appraisal report
Minutes of the incorporators' meeting or written subscription record
Written consents of directors and statutory auditor
Corporate name availability confirmation or search result
Power of attorney and identification of the filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, cure the stated omission within the statutory correction period and resubmit the amended documents. If the application is rejected because of an unavailable corporate name or defective address, change the name or move the registered office and file a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration, tax identification, and corporate bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office, filed online through Hometax; municipal tax authority for local registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation registration, the Representative Director shall, within the statutory filing window, submit the business registration application to the National Tax Service district office having jurisdiction over the registered office. This step obtains the corporate taxpayer identification number and the Business Registration Certificate, enabling invoicing, value-added tax compliance, wage reporting, and opening of permanent corporate bank accounts. If the shareholders include non-residents, the Company must file the relevant foreign investment report with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or its delegated bank before or within the time prescribed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, in order to obtain remittance and tax treaty benefits. The Company shall also complete local municipal tax registration and register employees for employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance at the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service.
required_dossiers: Corporation Registration Certificate issued by the court registry
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and certified copy
Business registration application form
Corporate seal certificate and representative director identification
Lease contract and owner consent for the registered office
Corporate bank account details or temporary account certificate
Foreign investment report declaration, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the application because the corporate object appears to include regulated activities, provide the ISIC 7490 and NAICS 541930 professional-services description and revise the tax registration statements. If business registration is filed late, submit a voluntary disclosure and request penalty mitigation. If the foreign investment report is missing, file it immediately with the delegated bank to preserve treaty protections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; ISIC 7490 and NAICS 541930 cover multilingual translation, localization, and media dubbing as professional office-based services, not manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. No industrial licensing board or municipal industrial agency clearance is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; no statutory manufacturing or operating permit is required. The only operational authorization is the standard Business Registration Certificate issued by the National Tax Service after incorporation registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environmental Corporation would become relevant only if the Company later establishes a physical production studio, warehouse, or other facility subject to environmental permitting.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; no EIA classification tier is assigned for a pure localization and translation office. If a physical studio or warehouse is later added, the project must be screened under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and may be classified as an Environmental Registration or Full EIA depending on floor area, location, and activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; zero industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound, or hazardous waste thresholds are triggered by multilingual translation, software localization, or dubbing project management. Ordinary commercial office waste and e-waste must be disposed of through licensed municipal waste contractors in compliance with the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable; no fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required for a professional office under the Fire Services Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act beyond the landlord's compliance with building fire-safety regulations. If the Company later operates a physical dubbing studio, recording facility, or equipment storage area, it must obtain a civil-defense fire prevention certificate from the local fire station and comply with the workplace safety requirements of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first determine whether it has a domestic place of business in Korea; if not, it must appoint a Korean tax representative. The entity then files a business registration application with the competent district tax office through HomeTax, attaching its certificate of incorporation, overseas business registration certificate, board resolution, and power of attorney for the tax representative. The NTS issues the Korean business registration number, which functions as the statutory TIN and VAT ID. For foreign suppliers of digital services or localization services to Korean consumers, a simplified VAT registration may be filed through HomeTax under the foreigner business registration procedure. After issuance, the entity must register its tax invoice issuing credentials and e-tax invoice program with NTS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa; entity-level taxation is mandatory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover de minimis for VAT registration; registration is required from the commencement of taxable supplies. The simplified taxpayer regime applies to eligible small vendors with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000. Foreign non-resident suppliers with Korean place of supply are also required to register regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoice issuance is mandatory for all VAT-taxable business-to-business supplies. Invoices must be issued through the HomeTax portal or a certified electronic tax invoice system and transmitted to NTS no later than the day following issuance. NTS applies near-real-time validation through API-based e-invoice submission, and retail sales to individuals are generally evidenced by cash receipts or credit card sales slips transmitted to authorized payment clearing houses. There is no separate real-time anti-fraud digital stamping model; the electronic tax invoice clearance is achieved through mandatory digital transmission to NTS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods must be physically removed from Korea and shipped to a foreign purchaser under a Korean Customs Service export declaration. Localization, translation, media dubbing, and related services qualify for zero rating when supplied to a non-resident business or non-resident customer for use wholly outside Korea, evidencing by written contract, invoice, and foreign currency settlement. International transport and directly related supporting services also qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korean Customs Service electronic export declaration via UNI-PASS (equivalent to an export bill of entry)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB)
Commercial invoice and localization/dubbing service contract
Bank foreign exchange transaction certificate or inward remittance certificate equivalent showing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Overseas client documentation confirming non-resident status and use of delivered digital content or localization outputs outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and the Korean Customs Service jointly cross-check export declarations, customs loading records, transport documents, and bank remittance trails. If the zero-rate claim is not substantiated by the required customs and foreign exchange documentation, or if export proceeds are not repatriated by the 180-day deadline, the zero rate is reversed and VAT at 10% is assessed on the supply, together with statutory VAT surcharges ranging from 10% to 40% of the deficient tax. Willful evasion or issuance of false tax invoices additionally gives rise to criminal penalties, customs penalties, and a retrospective clawback of any input VAT credits previously recovered on zero-rated export inputs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK); Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and Korea Customs Service act as co-applying authorities under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised current-account regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current-account receipts and payments for goods, services and royalties are generally free and require ex-post reporting rather than licensing. The Korean won is not globally fully convertible due to capital-account controls; all cross-border capital transactions require either prior declaration, registration, or reporting to the licensed foreign-exchange bank or BOK. Equity capital contributions from non-residents must be reported through the reinvestment and foreign-investment notification framework under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the investment meets the statutory thresholds. Surplus funds cannot simply be remitted as dividends without corporate tax filing and a BOK foreign-exchange declaration; profit remittance is permitted after audited financial statements and dividend approval, subject to withholding tax and tax clearance evidence. Export proceeds must be received within 18 months from the date of export, may be held in foreign-currency bank accounts, and are subject to deposit reporting; there is no forced conversion of export proceeds to KRW, but when conversion occurs it must be executed at a market rate through a licensed foreign-exchange bank with the appropriate transaction purpose code. The practical constraint for a localization agency is not convertibility fears but the need to document every inbound and outbound cross-border movement and maintain transaction-level files for BOK and tax audits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and BOK notifications, export earnings must be collected and deposited within 18 months from the date of export, with extensions available under BOK approval; there is no mandatory fixed percentage of Korean won conversion, meaning the mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0%, exporters may hold 100% of proceeds in foreign-currency accounts at domestic licensed banks, and any voluntary conversion must be at market rates through a licensed foreign-exchange bank and reported using the applicable BOK transaction-purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account and Cross-border FX Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary entity accounts. Wise and Payoneer can be used only as ancillary payout or collection rails outside Korea where they hold regulated licenses, but they are not chartered banks in the Republic of Korea and are not recognised under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act as substitutes for a statutory corporate bank account. A Chusik Hoesa is expected to maintain its domestic operating account, capital escrow facility and FX settlement at a Korean commercial bank. Domestic fintech providers must be licensed as electronic financial business operators; foreign EMIs therefore cannot be lawfully relied upon as the primary treasury, capital-verification or cross-border settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks generally require the authorised signing director or a duly appointed representative to appear physically at the branch for first onboarding, especially for corporations with foreign shareholding. Remote consular proxy opening is not a general fallback. A notarized and apostilled or consularised power of attorney together with a certified board resolution may be conditionally accepted for isolated administrative steps, but the signatory and ultimate beneficial owners are expected to complete live video KYC or an in-branch interview; refusal to appear or a purely remote offshore incorporation posture materially raises AML risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-director real-name and tax residency mismatch between shareholder register, passport and bank signature records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport copy, Alien Registration Card or equivalent Korean foreigner identity record, tax residence certificate, certified board resolution appointing the signatory, corporate seal certificate, and notarized power of attorney if the onboarding representative is different from the director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership and multi-layered ownership chain opacity, especially with non-resident holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Articles of Incorporation, current shareholder register, signed UBO declaration identifying each natural person with at least 25% ownership or control, corporate chain org chart to the ultimate natural person, passport copies of all UBOs, and signed confirmation of no political exposure status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction purpose mismatch and insufficient commercial substance for a multilingual localization and media dubbing company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed localization service agreements, itemised invoices, proof of office lease or co-working space in Korea, Korean business registration certificate, website and domain ownership evidence, client onboarding documents, prior period financial statements where available, and descriptive workflow documentation showing source and target language operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concern on inbound capital injection from non-resident shareholder or related party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the remitting bank, board minutes approving share issuance or capital contribution, capital contribution agreement, foreign-investment report acknowledgment from BOK or the designated foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and a certified funding affidavit showing the investor's lawful source of wealth.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for a Chusik Hoesa must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's account to the beneficiary's won or foreign-currency capital escrow account designated at a licensed Korean bank. The remittance instruction must include the Korean bank's SWIFT address, beneficiary legal name exactly as registered with the bank, investor legal name, and the BOK transaction-purpose code for inward remittance or foreign investment capital. The receiving bank must issue a Certificate of Inward Remittance before the funds are moved from escrow into operating liquidity. If the injection qualifies as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the company or investor must submit a foreign-investment report to the designated foreign-exchange bank or BOK before or within the statutory period after receipt, using the capital/equity classification rather than a current-transfer classification. The capital verification procedure requires the bank certificate, the revised shareholder register, board minutes and the registered entity's statutory seal acknowledgement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the localization agency should be executed through the domestic bank's corporate FX platform using SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for service and settlement invoices. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are intended for physical trade in goods and are not the correct clearing rail for professional multilingual translation or media dubbing services. For each outbound service payment, the bank will require the underlying service agreement, an itemised invoice, proof of the recipient bank, and the BOK service-transaction purpose code. Where the payment crosses with-a-holding-tax jurisdictions, the bank may require evidence of withholding tax filing or the applicable tax treaty before remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts with an onshore licensed Korean FX bank, permitted where the notional amount does not exceed the documented underlying receivable or payable arising from localization service contracts or foreign-currency capital exposure, with the forward tenor aligned to the actual expected settlement date.

Foreign-exchange swaps between KRW and USD are permissible for matching funding gaps, provided each leg corresponds to a real transaction such as an upcoming service settlement or a capital remittance, and the swap is not used to build speculative open positions.

Cross-currency swaps are permitted only when the Chusik Hoesa has an actual foreign-currency debt or investment position with notional and repricing terms matching the base transaction, and where BOK notification or registration is completed in advance if the underlying transaction crosses the regulatory threshold.

KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not an acceptable onshore hedging tool for the Korean-resident operating entity; NDFs are primarily offshore instruments and may be treated as speculative or circumventing Korean FX rules. Onshore hedging must be settled through a domestic licensed bank and continuously supported by underlying transaction evidence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) resolution, financial statement approval, and statutory minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a regulator; retained in the statutory records of the company at its registered office and subject to inspection by the Commercial Court, National Tax Service, or Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year (for a December 31 fiscal year end, by March 31 of the following year); a different fiscal year end follows the same three-month statutory rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within three months exposes the company to administrative fines under Commercial Act Article 635(1) of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,750); the court may additionally order the meeting to be convened, and unapproved financial statements cannot be used to close the fiscal year without penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and local income tax surtax return, including required financial statement schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system; local income tax components are filed through the provincial or municipal tax portal as integrated in HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; the deadline is extended by one month to four months if a qualified tax accountant or certified public accountant prepares the return and the company has engaged a third-party preliminary audit or qualified tax agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underreporting triggers a 10% to 40% surcharge depending on the non-disclosure or underreporting classification, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% on unpaid tax; repeated or willful non-filing may lead to asset seizure, criminal prosecution, and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration of re-appointed or newly appointed directors and statutory auditor (if any) following the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Court (Beopwon) of the local district court where the registered office of the company is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the date of the AGM resolution appointing or re-appointing directors or the statutory auditor; if the resolution is effective as of the AGM, the two-week period runs from the resolution date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration is subject to a negligence fine of up to KRW 1,000,000 (approximately USD 750) under the Commercial Registration Act; until registration is completed, the appointed director cannot validly act against third parties, and the company may lose protection against unauthorized acts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual report on foreign ownership status and business performance (applicable if the company has non-resident shareholders or qualifies as a foreign-invested enterprise)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the foreign exchange bank designated by the foreign investor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the close of the fiscal year or within 90 days as prescribed by the Enforcement Decree of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; for calendar-year companies, the filing is generally due by March 31 or earlier depending on the designated bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual foreign-investment report may incur a fine of up to KRW 1,000,000 (approximately USD 750) and may cancel tax abatement or foreign-investment benefits; continued non-compliance may trigger administrative investigation and sanctions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and independent auditor report submitted to the financial regulator (mandatory only when the company meets the statutory external audit threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART) or the designated office supervising external audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end, or immediately after shareholder approval if the AGM occurs later; in no case may the audited statements be withheld beyond the statutory deadline applicable to compulsory audited companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or false submission can result in FSS administrative penalties, rejection or suspension of the audit report, and criminal fines under the External Audit Act of up to KRW 100 million (approximately USD 75,000) for material violations; the company may also be barred from selling or transferring the audited financial statements as legally valid documents

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Enforcement Decree of the External Audit Act, an external CPA audit is compulsory for: (a) every listed company; (b) any unlisted Chusik Hoesa whose total assets as of the previous fiscal year end exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); and (c) any company specifically designated by the Financial Services Commission due to public interest, high external borrowing, or dominance in the securities market. For a non-listed localization agency, the decisive quantitative test is the balance-sheet asset threshold of KRW 120 billion? Correcting to KRW 120 hundred million? Actually the threshold is KRW 12,000,000,000 (twelve billion Korean won, i.e., approximately USD 9,000,000). If total assets exceed this level, a registered CPA audit firm must audit the financial statements regardless of turnover or headcount. There is no separate turnover or headcount trigger for general non-listed corporations under the current external audit rules, but the Financial Services Commission may lower the threshold to KRW 10,000,000,000 for certain high-risk industries. All compulsory audit clients must use an accounting firm registered with the FSS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For Korean business entities, the applicable accounting framework is Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies, financial institutions, and compulsory-audit companies that meet the asset threshold; non-listed companies below the threshold may apply the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Enterprises. For consolidated or intercompany cross-border structures, K-IFRS or the local GAAP of the ultimate parent may be required, but the statutory base for a standalone Korean entity remains K-GAAP or K-IFRS as elected under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public UBO register for ordinary private companies. However, under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested company must annually confirm its foreign ownership and ultimate investor details by filing the foreign-invested enterprise annual report with KOTRA or its designated foreign exchange bank within the applicable statutory window (commonly 30-90 days after fiscal year end). For domestic share transfers, no annual UBO filing is due to the commercial register, but the company must update the shareholders ledger within a reasonable period after notification of transfer; if the transfer involves a foreign investor, the foreign exchange bank must be notified within 30 days of the transaction. Additionally, under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, financial institutions must perform customer due diligence to identify the ultimate beneficial owner when opening accounts or executing transactions exceeding KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500). Companies are required to maintain accurate beneficial ownership information in their internal registers and respond to requests from the financial intelligence unit within the statutory response period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages (if any)
Minute Book of AGM and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per year for a registered business address or compliance agent in Seoul/Busan; if a full corporate secretarial service including AGM administration and regulatory filings is engaged, the range is USD 1,000 - USD 3,500 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a voluntary or statutory CPA audit of a small non-listed localization agency with annual revenue below USD 10 million; USD 20,000 - USD 50,000 per year if the company has significant intercompany transactions, multi-currency revenue, or satisfies the compulsory external audit threshold requiring K-IFRS and FSS filing procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate; progressive Korean corporate income tax rates are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, 21% over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% over KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No Korean patent box regime; available incentives include R&D tax credits, employment and investment tax credits, foreign-invested enterprise tax reductions, and free economic zone incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, subject to statutory caps and qualifying activity requirements

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean corporate income tax return (Form 11 framework and attached schedules) filed by the Chusik Hoesa on the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal at hometax.go.kr; a foreign-controlled Korean entity with a domestic place of business files the standard corporate return for a domestic corporation together with international transaction summaries
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year; a December 31 year-end corporation must file by March 31 of the following year, and a short statutory extension may be available to foreign corporations only with prior NTS authorization

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and head office / domestic place of business registration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration number of the Chusik Hoesa and the address of the place of effective management; disclose all ultimate foreign shareholders and the existence of any overseas payment rails such as Wise B2B or Payoneer; appoint and disclose a Korean domestic tax representative if there is no resident director

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year declaration and filing status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the return as the annual final return; state the fiscal year-end date plainly and confirm whether the company is a resident Korean corporation for tax purposes; do not check foreign corporation branch status if the entity is a locally incorporated Chusik Hoesa

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Korean-source revenue, total income, and tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue from multilingual translation, professional localization, media dubbing, and project management services performed for Korean counterparties, including receipts collected through Wise B2B or Payoneer; apply arm's length transfer pricing to intercompany charges; add back non-deductible fees such as unjustified shareholder management charges; attach the international related-party transaction schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and progressive corporate income tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% progressive brackets to taxable income; for a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa, report worldwide taxable income unless foreign tax credits or DTA provisions exempt specific income; do not claim treaty exemptions unless a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement are in the file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, interim prepayments, and final corporate tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim interim corporate tax prepayments, foreign tax credits, and qualified incentive credits; attach evidence of foreign withholding taxes if claiming DTA credit relief; any mismatch between revenue on the financial statements and revenue reported may trigger an electronic tax invoice cross-check and NTS desk audit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retained earnings and outbound dividend withholding declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show distributable profit and the amount intended for foreign shareholders; for any dividend to a non-resident, the company is the withholding agent and must apply the statutory 22% effective withholding tax or a treaty-reduced rate only after the prescribed treaty relief form is approved; failure to withhold creates personal recovery exposure for the representative director

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file on time triggers additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent non-filing; underreporting triggers 10% additional tax, increased to 40% if the understatement is by dishonest means; late payment accrues at approximately 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount; criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax, with NTS authority to make arbitrary assessment when no proper return is filed

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% effective statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, composed of 20% national corporate withholding tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax; the rate may be reduced by an applicable bilateral tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Korean payer must obtain before payment a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign shareholder's resident tax authority, a signed beneficial ownership declaration, and the prescribed NTS application for reduction/exemption of withholding tax; the foreign recipient must satisfy the treaty's limitation-on-benefits or principal purpose test; if the treaty relief package is incomplete, the company must withhold at the 22% statutory rate and the non-resident may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 22% effective (20% national tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge); bilateral DTA protocols commonly reduce interest to 10% to 15% and royalties to 0% to 15%, with a zero rate available for certain categories only when the recipient meets the beneficial ownership and Korean-source substantive documentation conditions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion in annual cross-border related-party transactions generally triggers the Local File and Master File documentation requirement, with lower category-specific thresholds for service and financial transactions; all cross-border related-party dealings must also be reported through the annual corporate tax return international transaction summary
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Core Income-Generating Activities concept is enforced through substance-over-form judicial doctrine, controlled foreign company rules, and the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test; the Chusik Hoesa must maintain real employees, office space, board decisions, client contracts, invoicing, and quality control for localization and dubbing services in Korea, otherwise the tax authority may disregard the entity as a conduit, deny treaty benefits, and recharacterize income as Korean-source business income

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through unreported overseas payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors arrange for overseas clients to remit localization, translation, dubbing, and project-management fees into Wise B2B or Payoneer accounts in foreign PSP names without recording the receipts in the Korean Chusik Hoesa books, and the cash is retained offshore or withdrawn as purported non-taxable loans
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, fraudulent non-filing or underreporting attracts additional tax of 40% of the evaded corporate tax, plus late-payment surcharges of about 0.03% per day; the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act authorizes imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to three times the evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil where the Chusik Hoesa is an alter ego of its shareholders; the representative director and signatory officers are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax under the Korean Commercial Act, and the NTS may attach personal assets, impose travel bans, and blacklist the directors during criminal tax investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company lacking economic substance and abusing treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity has no office, no local employees, no independent decision-making, and no billing substance; it merely routes IP royalties through a foreign shell parent and claims treaty-exempt status on payments while the true management and client-facing localization activities remain outside Korea
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement under anti-avoidance rules and the OECD MLI principal purpose test, deny the DTA benefits, impute the full Korean-source profit to the Chusik Hoesa, and impose a 40% additional tax for dishonest underreporting together with penalty interest; the foreign shareholder may become secondarily liable for the unpaid assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director who signs false substance declarations, boards resolutions, or DTA benefit forms can be treated as a co-principal in tax evasion; civil joint liability follows under Commercial Act Article 401, with criminal exposure of imprisonment up to 5 years, fines, travel bans, and disqualification from serving as a Korean corporate director

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing and disguised profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean corporation invoices related foreign affiliates below cost for localization services, buys duplicative head office support at excessive markups, or borrows from the foreign shareholder through a thin capital structure and pays inflated intercompany interest leaving no Korean taxable income while cash is repatriated as interest or dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may reassess the taxpayer under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs using an approved arm's length method, deny interest deductions, apply the 10% or 40% understatement penalty depending on fraudulent intent, and impose daily late-payment surcharges; failure to produce transfer pricing documentation allows the NTS to estimate taxable income by default methodology
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve false intercompany agreements and intentionally ignore transfer pricing rules are personally liable for the tax shortfall when the corporate form is disregarded; in egregious cases, the prosecutor can indict the directors under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the court may impose personal asset seizure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment up to 5 years
